## 12. Bloodlines and Canon Connections

### Cormor Dream-Eater → the Cormorian Royal Dynasty → Osrid and Rhydia `[LOCKED]`

- **Cormor Dream-Eater** is the founder of the Cormorian royal dynasty (Section 2 — The Cormorian founding myth)
- A legendary brigand who lived in the pre-Empire era of what is now Cormoria
- Sealed an ancient evil bird Pokemon whose name is "lost to all history" (author's note: this is **Phancero**, the cross-fandom glitch bird reference; never named in-game)
- Uncovered a metal containment chamber containing what would become known as **Justice** (a shiny Iron Valiant from a distant future, mistaken for an evolved Ralts-demigod)
- Used these two events to legitimize his establishment of a dynasty
- **Direct ancestor of Empress Pierra Cormoria I, Queen-Regent Rhydia, and Prince Osrid** through the matrilineal Cormoria royal line
- The country took its name from him: **Cormor → Cormoria** (his name became the dynastic and territorial name)

**The thematic weight of this lineage:**

The Cormorian royal family's "Arceus-blessed surname-bestowal authority" (Section 2 — Cormorian surnames as sacrament) is built on a **mythologized history of what was originally bandit-establishment.** The royal family's divine authority is a *self-mythologized post-hoc narrative* by the descendants of a brigand who got lucky.

This silently justifies Osrid's eventual renunciation arc (Section 5). When Osrid chooses to discard the prince-identity and live as Veddev in Paldea, he is in some sense *returning to the family's truth* — that royal identity is contingent and earned-through-circumstance, not divine and inherited-by-blood. **The dynasty was never as Arceus-blessed as it claims. Osrid's renunciation is a quiet act of historical honesty.**

Rhydia continues the matrilineal Cormorian royal line through her future descendants. Osrid's line passes through *adoption* into the Amber-Letz family (Vandras's adoption of Veddev), producing the Berlitz lineage culminating in Volo and Cynthia. **The bloodline splits at Osrid's renunciation:**
- **Rhydia's biological line** continues the matrilineal Cormorian royal legacy (which probably ends with the empire's eventual collapse — both DM and the present-day Pokemon canon have no obvious Cormorian-empire continuation)
- **Osrid's adopted line** (the Amber-Letz/Berlitz family) produces the more historically significant modern-canon descendants
- Sister and brother, both lost to history in different ways

### The Five-Oldest Noble Houses of Cormoria — and Ashland's exceptional status `[LOCKED v0.9.8]`

Cormoria's noble House structure has *gradations of antiquity.* The empire's recognized noble Houses span centuries of accumulated history, but **five Houses are recognized as the absolute oldest** — the families whose names were among the first formally bestowed when the empire codified its noble structure (Section 2 — Cormorian surnames and the Arceus-blessing irrevocability rule).

**The five-oldest Houses, in order of name-bestowal:**

1. **House Langerin** — keepers of the Mirroh Necropolis (the sealed gate to Distortion World; Section 7 — Kimaris Langerin). Occult-traditional naming convention. Generational Marshadow ace.
2. **House Nightfall** — Osrid and Rhydia's paternal house; Osrid is half-Nightfall by patriline. Dark-type tradition; a long bloodline of military commanders and intelligence officers. **In steep decline at game start.** Full family tree `[LOCKED v0.9.8]`:
   - **Mordred Nightfall** — patriarch; former Trial Baron (10 years) then **Champion of Cormoria for 50 years**, defeated by his 15-year-old granddaughter Rhydia 5 years pre-game (the loss was partly 50 years' weariness; his peak skill was so immense even the best 15-year-old couldn't have beaten him at full power). **Childhood friend and lifelong rival of Falco Raptora** (Section 7 — Falco) — the two were the strongest trainers of their generation, both with immense vitality. **The Falco-Mordred parallel is a deliberate authored mirror:** two ancient patriarchs of two five-oldest Houses, two failure modes of the same generational position — *Falco clings* (refuses to retire or name an heir at 100), *Mordred collapsed* (forced out by Rhydia, retired to the estate, watched his House decline). Falco may be refusing to become Mordred.
   - **Eldred Nightfall** — Mordred's younger son; self-taught Dark-type prodigy; youngest-ever to reach Tarasque rank before 20; defeated his tutored older brother Dantalion in a public match to become the face of House Nightfall; married Pierra and became Prince-Consort; **assassinated by Baradus 10 years pre-game** (the catalyst for the Widening Eye's four-way split and the Swords of Ruin's rise — Section 8). Father of Osrid and Rhydia.
   - **Dantalion "Dan" Nightfall** — Mordred's elder son, the once-chosen heir; humiliated by Eldred's public defeat; fled into self-exile as Cormoria's diplomat to Kalos after Eldred's assassination. Never appears on-screen; referenced in dialogue only.
   - **Leah Alban Nightfall** — Dantalion's wife, married in from **House Alban** (the Grass-type Trial 6 House) — an example of how deeply Cormoria's old Houses have intermarried over time. Emotionally collapsed during her daughter's upbringing. **Note:** House Alban is *destroyed* during the Trial 6 chapter — corrupted by Wo-Chien (planted by Baradus), its scion Indrid driven to massacre the family (Section 7 — Indrid Alban). **Leah, by virtue of having married into House Nightfall, may be the last surviving Alban by blood** — `[OPEN]` whether this is dramatically significant or simply a quiet fact. House Alban is *not* one of the five-oldest Houses; it was a significant agricultural-and-conservation noble house whose factional divisions made it vulnerable to cult infiltration.
   - **Bridget Nightfall** — Dantalion and Leah's daughter; Osrid and Rhydia's first cousin; born exactly 10 years before the twins (age 30 at game start); the **7th Trial Baroness (Dark)**; matriarch-by-default of the declining house; older-sister figure to Rhydia across the 10 post-assassination years. See Section 7 — Bridget Nightfall.
3. **House Moray** — Psychic-type tradition; Silas, Brie, and Domdaniel (Section 7 — Brie Moray, Silas Moray).
4. **House Umbra** — Latin-shadow naming tradition; Vizier of Education; Joustroll/Jousteel heraldic line (Section 7 — Cadmus Umbra; Section 9 — Joustroll/Jousteel Line).
5. **House Raptora** — Flying-type tradition; pioneered the Braviary mount infrastructure and the Bombirdier postal/aerial-delivery network across the continent (Section 7 — Falco Raptora; subsection below).

**The Ashland exception `[LOCKED v0.9.8 — expands the v0.9.4 Naljo-Ashland lore at lines 164-168 below]`:**

**House Ashland is *about as old* as Langerin and Nightfall** in terms of family lineage age — *but they are not counted among the five-oldest because they came to Cormoria with their family name already established.* The other five had their names *bestowed* by the empire as part of the formal noble-codification event (the Arceus-blessing ritual that makes Cormorian surnames irrevocable; Section 2). **Ashland brought their pre-existing Naljo name with them and the empire honored it.**

This makes Ashland a *uniquely-situated* House:

- Their *bloodline* age is in the same tier as the five-oldest
- Their *Cormorian noble status* postdates the original five
- **They are functionally a sixth "ancient House" — but structurally a *recent-arriving* House** in terms of empire-recognition timing

**The Naljo backstory (expanded from v0.9.4 lore at lines 164-168):**

House Ashland originated in **Naljo** — the region setting of the *Pokémon Naljo* fan project series (Brown/Prism). They were known there as a **literally pyrokinetic family** — humans able to physically conjure and direct fire, not merely train Fire-type Pokémon. The "divine family of Fire magic users" framing is *not* metaphor; the family carries real supernatural fire-conjuring ability through their bloodline. **They were cast out from Naljo by Varaneous, one of several major legendaries that guard the wild lands of Naljo** — alongside several other Naljo legendaries also expelled in the same period. The lore around Naljo is *background texture* in our game, not load-bearing plot — mentioned in passing where relevant; not expanded into a major Naljo subsection.

**`[v0.9.8 ADDITION]` The cast-out reason — the family's foundational moral act:** Varaneous was a deeply isolationist legendary who *killed any humans approaching Naljo* (literally burning down ships of arrivals) and *enforced his will against humans already living in Naljo*, including burning dissenters alive. **Varaneous wanted to use the Ashland family's unique pyrokinetic power as instruments of this isolationist violence** — directing them to materialize fire to launch fireballs at incoming ships, and to mobilize Ashland family members as *enforcers* who would burn people alive on Varaneous's command to keep human Naljo-dwellers in line and punish dissenters. **The Ashland family turned away from this violence.** They refused to be made into Varaneous's executioners of other humans. The cast-out was the *consequence of moral refusal*, not theological heresy or political disobedience in the conventional sense. **The family's founding moral act was refusing to burn people alive at a tyrant-legendary's direction.** This single act of refusal is the foundation of House Ashland's identity across all subsequent generations. They left Naljo as moral refugees, brought their pyrokinetic legacy to Cormoria (Section 7 — Reid Ashland; Section 7 — Sable Ashland), and rebuilt as a noble house whose deepest character is *the refusal to make fire serve human-on-human violence.*

**`[v0.9.8 ADDITION]` Pyrokinesis in the modern family — diminished but still living:** The pyrokinetic legacy *has diminished* across most modern Ashland branches; most members of the broader family no longer have *active* fire-conjuring ability, only the affinity for Fire-type Pokemon that comes from carrying the bloodline. **The determining factor each generation of who leads the family is who has the strongest pyrokinetic legacy and the deepest bond-potential with Fire-type Pokemon.** The succession rule is *strict*. **Reid Ashland is the first family member in a generation since his uncle Sable to be born with *active* pyrokinetic powers.** This is why leadership fell to Reid immediately after Sable's disappearance — not by birth-order default but by the family's strict succession rules (Section 7 — Reid Ashland). Reid's three younger sisters (Rain, Brook, River) lack pyrokinesis and were never candidates by family rule. The pyrokinetic legacy is genuinely *rare in the modern era* — these are the *only two* living Ashland family members with active powers.

**`[v0.9.8 ADDITION]` The treason-suspicion historical irony:** When Cormorian common knowledge after Eldred's assassination crystallized as "House Ashland probably helped assassinate Eldred Nightfall", the people repeating this slander **were ignorant of the family's actual Naljo history**. Most Cormorians don't know House Ashland's founding moral identity — they treat them as just another long-standing noble house. **They cannot articulate what they are getting wrong about the family because they do not know.** The family that *fled Naljo because they refused to be made instruments of violence against innocents* is now suspected of having abetted exactly such violence — and the people slandering them would *change their minds* if they understood. **The historical ignorance is itself part of the tragedy.**

After the exile, the Ashland family migrated. They eventually settled in Cormoria, bringing with them:
- **Their family name** (which the empire honored rather than re-bestowing)
- **Their deep Fire-magic tradition** (which became House Ashland's Fire-type Trial-House mastery in Cormoria)
- **Their accumulated combat and craft knowledge** from their Naljo period
- **The latent shame of exile** — they are an *exiled-aristocracy* family making good in a new empire, and the family's quiet relationship to this displacement is part of their character (Section 7 — Reid Ashland's "decade of public service to defend his family's reputation" arc echoes this generational positioning)

**Sable Ashland's displacement-and-return arc** (Section 7 — Sable Ashland) takes on a deeper resonance against this background: Sable is the Ashland who is *literally displaced again*, this time temporally rather than geographically — *the family that was exiled from Naljo produces a son who is exiled from his own present.* And Sable's eventual return to a Cormoria where his childhood friends (the Sylphons) have rearranged their lives carries echoes of the Ashland founders' arrival in Cormoria centuries earlier — *coming back to find the world changed.*

**House Raptora's empire-service legacy `[LOCKED v0.9.8]`:**

House Raptora is the youngest of the five-oldest Houses but became one of the empire's most operationally important. Two specific infrastructures were *engineered by House Raptora* and have shaped Cormorian everyday life across centuries:

- **The Braviary mount system.** House Raptora *pioneered* the breeding-and-training program that produces Cormoria's distinctive Braviary partner-Pokemon — the Normal/Flying *honest civic-service form* that became the empire's national bird and cultural icon (Section 9 — Braviary Inter-City Travel System). Raptora's centuries of selective breeding established the Braviary line as it is currently known across the empire. **The Templar Arceus order operationalizes the system as a public service** (citizens pay Templars at city Taverns for inter-city Braviary flights), but the engineering substrate is Raptora's. *This means House Raptora is upstream of the Templars' Braviary partnership without being part of the Templar order itself.* It is a quiet structural relationship — the Templars *manage* what Raptora *built*.
- **The Bombirdier postal and aerial-delivery service.** A *specially-bred Bombirdier line*, engineered by House Raptora across generations, that runs the empire's inter-continental postal and package-delivery infrastructure. **This is genuinely new lore as of v0.9.8** — the Bombirdier service was not previously documented; Falco Raptora's character entry establishes it as the family's signature *commercial* contribution to the empire (parallel to House Sylphon's mercantile guild contribution, House Surge's military/electrical contribution, etc.). The Bombirdier service is run by House Raptora directly, not delegated to a religious or civic intermediary the way Braviary travel is.

**The dual infrastructure (Braviary mounts + Bombirdier postal) gives House Raptora extraordinary *empire-wide informational reach.*** Raptora-affiliated personnel are present in every city, watching every routine flight, observing every package routed. **This reach is part of why Falco Raptora is so well-positioned to be a member of the covert Resistance Triad** (Section 7 — Falco Raptora). The Triad operates partly *because* one of its members has line-of-sight into the empire's everyday movement patterns at a granularity no Concordance member possesses.

`[OPEN]` Whether the cult crisis has begun *exploiting* Raptora infrastructure (forged postage, cult messengers using public Braviary travel, etc.) and whether Falco has had to take counter-measures
`[OPEN]` Whether the Bombirdier postal service has its own modern-canon descendant (parallel to Sylphon → Silph Co or Vandras → Berlitz family lineages), or whether it remains a Cormorian-empire-only institution
`[OPEN]` Whether the Bombirdier service has its own employees / hierarchy / specific recurring NPCs the player encounters across the game (recommendation: yes — postal workers / aerial-delivery couriers as recurring incidental NPC presence; one or two named recurring couriers as flavor)

### Vandras Amber-Letz → Volo → Cynthia `[LOCKED]`

- Vandras Amber-Letz finds Osrid post-cataclysm — **as a stranger, with no idea who Osrid is** — and takes him in out of pure compassion
- Vandras gives him the name **Veddev** and adopts him as a younger brother
- **Vandras never learns the truth.** He dies a stranger to the knowledge that his adoptive brother was the Prince of Cormoria. The greatest fan-project Pokemon family lineage we are establishing descends from a man whose adoptive family never knew his origin.
- Veddev and Eden's children become Vandras's grandchildren-by-adoption
- The Amber-Letz merchant guild grows across ~1,800 years
- Volo (PLA) is a descendant
- Cynthia (Gen 4) is a more distant descendant
- Family name evolves: Amber-Letz → Amberletz → … → **Berlitz**
- **Cynthia's canonical gravitas tracks with two millennia of bloodline carrying unspoken historical depth** — none of Veddev's descendants know about Cormoria, but the weight of *something* is passed forward in their family identity
- Implied through detail, not stated outright

### Glaive → Dragon's Den Order → Lance `[LOCKED — soft canon]`

- Glaive founds Blackthorn City and the Dragon's Den order in Johto
- Lance's family descends from the Dragon's Den order

- His nickname *Blackthorn* is the in-game hint

### Umbra → Professor Tenebris `[LOCKED — expanded v0.9.8]`

- Umbra's family preserves Latin-shadow naming tradition across ~2,000 years
- Tenebris (Dreamstone Mysteries) is a descendant
- Tied to scholarly/philosophical lineage
- **House Umbra's heraldic-symbol Pokemon line is Joustroll/Jousteel** (Water/Steel; full lore in Section 9 — The Joustroll/Jousteel Line). The line is Cormorian-exclusive — no other house, commoner, or foreign trainer has access — and the Umbra family's centuries-long cultivation of this line is what has anchored an Umbra at the Vizier-of-Education role across so much of Cormorian history. Heraldic symbol *and* structural source of the family's political durability across generations.
- **Cormorian engineered-weapons twin-pair narrative** (Section 9): four absent canonical legendaries (Zacian-Crowned, Zamazenta, Lunala, Solgaleo) have their signature moves repurposed as Cormorian-engineered weapons (Behemoth Blade, Behemoth Bash, Moongeist Beam, Sunsteel Strike) handed to the three starter lines + Tinkaton's Stage-3 Behemoth Bash. The thematic statement: *Cormorian engineering surpasses legendary gifts.* House Umbra's centuries-old Jousteel cultivation is the *living tradition* parallel to this engineering achievement — both are demonstrations of the Cormorian conviction that *partnership and craft can rival cosmic-tier resources.* Where the engineered weapons exist as moves in starter learnsets, House Umbra's contribution exists as the living Joustroll bloodline itself. **Same thematic, different medium.**
- After Cormoria's collapse, the Jousteel line presumably ceases to exist anywhere in the modern Pokemon world *unless* Tenebris-line descendants preserved seed-stock from the family cultivation tradition. `[OPEN]` whether this is canonical to the DM-era continuity.

### Boran Surge → Lt. Surge of Vermillion City `[LOCKED — soft canon]`

- Boran Surge, the Cormorian Windshear-rank officer who served as Osrid's combat mentor, fathered children with multiple Kanto natives during the Kanto-Johto-Hoenn war (Section 7 — Boran Surge)
- **One of those Kantoan descendants is the ancestor of Lt. Surge of Vermillion City** (canonical Kanto Gym Leader, Electric specialist, modern era)
- The Cormorian Empire's most morally compromised mentor seeded a Kanto lineage that eventually produces a partnership-thesis Pokemon trainer in the modern era. **The worst actions of the past sometimes produce the best people of the future.**
- Light touch — never stated explicitly in game, implied through worldbuilding details
- The Surge family of House Surge in Cormoria continues separately and is *not* directly connected to Lt. Surge's lineage — Lt. Surge descends from the half-Kanto branch, not the Cormorian noble branch

### Sylphon (of Sylphon & Stone) → Silph Co. of Kanto `[LOCKED — soft canon; expanded v0.9.8]`

- The Sylphon family is one of the two founding families of the Sylphon & Stone merchant guild (Section 2 — Sylphon & Stone)
- The guild's empire-era leadership at story start is jointly held by **Chairman Robard Sylphon** and his wife **Simone Sylphon** (Section 7 — Simone Sylphon; House Sylphon is also the Normal-type Trial House, with Simone as the 4th Trial Baroness — Section 4)
- **The Sylphon guild splintering — the historical mechanism by which Sylphon & Stone fractures `[LOCKED v0.9.8]`:** The Act IV Sylphon & Stone Exposure beat (Section 10 — Act IV) publicly reveals Robard Sylphon's facilitation of the Beads Cult's funding pipeline. Robard is forced to step down as Chairman; criminal proceedings and political fallout follow. **The shock cascades through the guild's organizational structure** — Sylphon-branch shareholders, lieutenants, regional managers, and trade-route operators react in factional disarray. Some publicly disavow the Sylphon name and renegotiate independent positions. Others retreat from Cormoria to regional commercial centers across the diminishing empire. The guild as a single Cormorian institution does not survive Robard's fall intact; the Sylphon branch *fragments,* and over the following decades the fragments seed themselves across the empire's territorial extent.
- **Simone Sylphon's Kalos departure `[LOCKED v0.9.8]`:** After Robard's exposure and forced resignation, Simone takes the unambiguous middle path — she **sells her shares in Sylphon & Stone, leaves Robard, and emigrates to Kalos**, where she founds her own merchant guild on her own terms. Her ultimate ending is left ambiguous; the bible *does not* commit to a canonical modern-era descendant entity for her Kalos guild. **Simone's Kalos lineage is *not* on the Sylphon → Silph Co descent path** — the Silph Co inheritance runs through whichever Sylphon-branch fragments remained in continental territory and reorganized after the splintering, not through Simone's clean break.
- Following the splintering and the wider Cormorian gradual decline across the post-empire centuries, **the descendants of those continental Sylphon-branch fragments eventually settle in Kanto**
- Across ~2,000 years of accumulated commercial expertise (built on Sylphon & Stone's empire-era specialization in Pokemon-goods), the Sylphon descendants eventually found **Silph Co.**
- Linguistic evolution: Sylphon → Sylph → Silph (millennial pronunciation drift)
- **Silph Co.** in modern canon is the dominant Pokemon-tech corporation of Kanto — responsible for the Master Ball, the Silph Scope, and various Pokemon-research technologies
- Neither Silph Co. nor canon Pokemon historians knows the corporation's Cormorian origin
- **Ironic structural note:** the Beads Cult's funding flowed through Sylphon & Stone during the cult crisis (Section 8 — Goma). Silph Co.'s ancestral guild was *compromised by a Pokemon-Treasure cult* — a fact 2000 years deep in the past that no canon source will ever acknowledge. **The v0.9.8 expansion sharpens this irony:** the *specific human being* whose decisions compromised the guild was Robard Sylphon, and the *specific human being* who broke from him to preserve her independent commercial integrity was his own wife Simone — and *neither* the disgraced husband's continental descendants (which become Silph Co) nor the wife's clean-break Kalos lineage (which becomes something the bible does not specify) acknowledges any of this 2000 years on.

### Stone (of Sylphon & Stone) → Devon Corporation of Hoenn `[LOCKED — soft canon]`

- The Stone family is the other founding family of the Sylphon & Stone merchant guild
- Following Cormoria's decline, **the descendants of the main Stone shareholders settle in Hoenn**
- Across ~2,000 years, the Stone descendants eventually found **Devon Corporation**
- The "Stone" name is preserved in the canonical Devon Corp character name **Mr. Stone** (President of Devon Corp in RSE/ORAS) and **Steven Stone** (Hoenn Champion of RSE/ORAS) — the family name carries forward across millennia, even as the company name drifts (Stone → Stoneward / regional adaptations → Devon, possibly from a geographic settlement name)
- **Devon Corporation** in modern canon is the dominant Pokemon-tech corporation of Hoenn — responsible for the Devon Scope, the PokeNav, various Hoenn-region Pokemon technologies
- Like Silph Co., Devon's Cormorian origin is not known to canon historians
- **Steven Stone** as the canonical Hoenn Champion thus carries a hidden Cormorian ancestral connection — his family was the empire-era largest merchant guild's commercial pillar. This is *delicious* layered canon-connection: a modern canon Champion descended from the Cormorian commercial elite, parallel to Cynthia descending from the Cormorian renounced prince.

### Cormoria as the Lost Mother-Region of Modern Pokémon Canon `[LOCKED]`

**Cumulative bloodline and institutional descent across canon Pokémon regions:**

The Cormorian Empire's collapse scatters its bloodlines and institutions across all the canonical regions. Modern Pokémon canon is, structurally, **the fragments of Cormoria reorganized into the regions the player has visited in canon games.** Cormoria is the *lost mother-region* of modern Pokemon canon.

The complete map of bloodlines and institutional descent (all locked as soft-canon):

**From the Cormorian royal-bloodline (renounced prince / Veddev):**
- Osrid → Veddev (adopted into Amber-Letz family in Paldea) → ~1800 years of Berlitz lineage → **Volo (Sinnoh, PLA)** and **Cynthia (Sinnoh, Gen 4)**

**From the Cormorian commercial elite:**
- Sylphon family of Sylphon & Stone → **Silph Co. (Kanto)**
- Stone family of Sylphon & Stone → **Devon Corporation (Hoenn)** and the **Stone family lineage** (President Stone, Steven Stone)
- Amber-Letz family (smaller competitor) → **Berlitz family** (via Veddev's adoption; merges with royal bloodline)

**From the Cormorian military/noble culture:**
- Boran Surge → Kanto descendants → **Lt. Surge (Kanto)** (Vermillion City Gym Leader)
- Glaive Blackthorn → Dragon's Den order in Johto → **Lance's family** (Indigo Plateau Elite Four; canonical dragon master tradition)

**From the Cormorian scholarly tradition:**
- Cadmus Umbra → Latin-shadow naming tradition across ~2000 years → **Professor Tenebris (DM era)**

**From the Cormorian institutional structure:**
- The 9 Trials + 4 Viziers + Champion structure → proto-template for the modern **8 Gyms + Elite Four + Champion** structure
- Cormorian meritocratic values → embedded in modern regional Pokemon League cultures
- Cormorian Mega Evolution policy → cultural attitudes toward Mega Evolution restriction (and the Aerodactylite as a singular relic, eventually circulated through other channels)
- Ruin Cult remnants → **Team Somber** and the **Detective Academy** (DM era)

**The thematic significance of Cormoria as mother-region:**

The Cormorian Empire dies. Pierra mourns. Rhydia governs a partially-collapsed state. Eventually, across centuries, Cormoria fades entirely from political existence. **But its people scatter, and they reach every region the player will ever visit.** Modern Pokemon canon — every Gym Leader, every Champion, every major corporation, every regional cultural touchstone — is *downstream* of the empire we are writing.

Most fan projects place themselves *parallel* to canon. **Dreamstone Ruination places itself *upstream*.** The project's central thesis (Pokemon-as-partners-not-weapons) reaches across two millennia to shape every region the player has ever experienced. **The work being done in our game retroactively shapes the meaning of every other Pokémon experience the player has ever had.**

This is the project's deepest ambition: not just to tell a self-contained story, but to *give canon a history* — to be the *origin* of the world modern players know. Cynthia's gravitas, Lt. Surge's partnership thesis, Lance's dragon tradition, Steven Stone's mineralogical-noble-class refinement, Silph and Devon's Pokemon-tech dominance — all of it traces back to *what happens in our game.*

Players who care about the canon connections receive a deeply layered experience. Players who don't still get a complete story. **The layered meaning is gift, not gate.**

### Ruin Cult remnants → Team Somber + Detective Academy `[LOCKED]`

- Cult remnants who maintained ideology → Team Somber (DM villains)
- Cult-defectors who turned to opposition → Detective Academy (DM institution)
- Eden may have been instrumental in the proto-detective tradition, alongside Veddev/Osrid post-Paldean-sealing — implied, not stated

### Cormorian institutions → Modern Pokémon League `[LOCKED]`

- Cormoria's 9 Trials + 4 Viziers + Champion structure is the proto-template for the modern 8 Gyms + Elite Four + Champion structure
- This transmission happens via cultural osmosis across ~1,500–2,000 years
- Cormorian meritocratic values displace KJH despotic dynasties
- Kalos and Hisui cultural contributions also shape the modern Pokémon world
- Cormoria as a state does not survive — but its ideas form the political framework of every modern region

### Mega Evolution as Cormorian technique discovered by House Jalviss `[LOCKED]`

Mega Evolution arrived in Cormoria through the **House Jalviss excavations** — they discovered the first Mega Stones in Cormorian caves and mountains. They were destroyed in a single accident when an excavated Aerodactylite triggered a Mega Evolution in an ancient sleeping Aerodactyl that destroyed them all (see Section 2 and Section 4).

This historical event:
- Established Mega Evolution as a Cormorian-known technique (not exclusively Kalosian from our universe's perspective; cultural exchange with post-AZ Kalos may also exist `[OPEN]`)
- Created Cormoria's *grave* cultural attitude toward Megas — they are powerful and dangerous
- Justified the empire's restriction of Mega Evolution to state-sanctioned figures only (Section 2 — Mega Evolution policy)
- Left the **Aerodactylite** as a singular relic in the Jalviss ruins, possibly the only Aerodactylite in the world (Section 9)

**The protagonist's access to Mega Baxcalibur** (if they chose Frigibax) is itself a marker of state-recognized authority — gifted as a coronation symbol post-unmasking (Section 6, Section 10).

This is `[LOCKED]` now — the Jalviss-clan-origin story replaces the earlier `[WORKING]` "Kalosian art that reached Cormoria" framing.

### Cross-fandom References — Other Fan Project Acknowledgements `[LOCKED]`

Dreamstone Ruination contains *small, respectful nods* to two beloved Pokémon fan projects. These are flavor touches that acknowledge other major fan works while keeping our project narratively independent. Neither project is constrained by our references; we are honoring them without making demands of them.

**Pokémon Empire / Tellius (via Baradus):**
- **Baradus** is from the **Yo'aki tribe of Tellius** — Tellius being the setting of the *Pokémon Empire* fan project (a long-running, politically-rich fan project with serious worldbuilding)
- His exile from his tribe and journey through Kanto to Cormoria is *briefly* referenced in late-game dialogue, never deeply explored — flavor depth, not a major worldbuilding thread
- He carries his oldest companion Guzzlord (from his Yo'aki past) and acquired Articuno during his Kanto period
- Light touch on the broader Tellius/Yo'aki cultural relationship to Ultra Beasts (implied but not committed)
- 1-2 minor in-world references possible (e.g., a Templar Arceus intel-gatherer or a Cormorian scholar who recognizes the Yo'aki name) — single touch only, kept contained to Baradus

**Pokémon Naljo / Naljo (via House Ashland):**
- **House Ashland** originates from **Naljo** — a region setting of the *Pokémon Naljo* fan project series (Brown/Prism)
- House Ashland are described as "a supposedly divine family of Fire magic users" who were **cast out from Naljo by that region's chief legendary, Varaneous**, for reasons left unstated in our game
- Migrated to Cormoria before the Cormorian dynasty existed; struck a bargain with the proto-Cormorian royal family for control of the volcanic Mt. Ceram region
- The Naljo connection is *quietly* present in House Ashland's worldbuilding (Section 4) but doesn't require the player to know about *Pokemon Naljo* — it works as in-world flavor on its own

**The pattern we are establishing:** Dreamstone Ruination is positioned as a fan-project that respectfully nods to other major fan-projects in our community. Neither Pokémon Empire nor Pokémon Naljo is constrained by our use; we use them as background flavor that adds depth to specific characters/houses without making demands of their universes. This is the *intent* documented here so future bible-readers understand it isn't accidental cross-contamination.

### Cogita → canonical PLA Celestica character `[LOCKED v0.9.4 — major cross-canon connection]`

**Cogita is Lethys's niece.** First-degree familial connection. The canonical Pokemon Legends: Arceus character Cogita — the mysterious, ageless, white-haired keeper of cosmic wisdom in canonical PLA-era Hisui — is **the niece of the Blue Moon Hermit (Sage Lethys of the Celestica)**.

**Per Section 7 — Blue Moon Hermit entry:**
- Cogita is Celestica by birth (her uncle Lethys's tribal heritage)
- Her longevity in canonical PLA is now explained — *Celestica baseline + pact-blessing-by-blood-relation-to-Lethys* (one degree removed from Cormor); Tier 2 longevity in the project's pact-extended longevity framework (Section 9)
- She was left behind when Lethys and Cormor departed on their pilgrimage to deal with Phancero; she has been the *waiting* family member across centuries
- Her hidden grove in canonical PLA-era Hisui is traceable to *Celestica ancestral territory* — possibly a remnant of the original nomadic-tribe lands

**This reframes canonical Cogita's PLA portrayal:**

When the canonical PLA player encounters Cogita, she is — in this project's cosmology — *the surviving family member of a cosmic-tier founding event whose participants left her two thousand years ago.* Her gentle wisdom, her cosmic perspective, her acceptance of long ages — *all of it is the temperament of someone who has lived through generational loss and chosen to maintain dignity and grace across centuries.*

**Implications for the "lost mother-region" framing:**

Cormoria was already established as the upstream source of modern Pokemon canon's bloodlines and corporations. **Now the project's lore also reaches into canonical PLA's Celestica tribe**, connecting the most ancient canonical Pokemon culture directly to the project's foundational cosmology. **The Celestica Trail, the Celestica statues, and the Celestica ruins in canonical PLA are *cultural descendants* of the pre-Cormorian nomadic-tribe tradition** that Lethys and Cormor came from.

**Important framing:** Ruination's Cogita-connection does *not* constrain canonical PLA. Cogita's canonical portrayal remains intact; Ruination simply *adds depth* to her backstory that engaged fans can integrate. Players who notice the connection are rewarded; players who don't still get a complete Cogita in canonical PLA.

`[OPEN]` Whether Cogita herself appears in any Dreamstone Ruination content. Most likely **no** — she is canonically a PLA-era character; Ruination takes place ~2000 years before SV, ~500 years before PLA-era Hisui. Cogita is alive but presumably distant during Ruination's era.

### The Celestica → Hisuian Celestica connection `[LOCKED v0.9.4]`

The **Celestica nomadic tribes** of Ruination's pre-Cormorian era are connected to the canonical PLA **Celestica** of Hisui. Lethys and Cormor came from these tribes; Cogita is their direct heir.

**Per Section 2 — Cormorian founding myth and Section 7 — Blue Moon Hermit:**

- The Celestica were the original tribal people who roamed the unnamed region that would become Cormoria
- They were decimated by Phancero in the cosmic-historical era
- The survivors *preserved the oral histories* of what truly happened — Phancero's nature, Cormor's vengeance, the pact, the inversion of the four objects
- Their oral tradition gradually died out across centuries following Cormoria's founding
- **Some Celestica continued to exist as a tribal culture across millennia** — appearing in canonical PLA as the ancient mountain-people of Hisui who built the Celestica Trail and statues and worshipped Arceus

**The connection makes canonical Celestica more meaningful:** the Celestica's Arceus-worship in canonical PLA traces directly back to the original partnership-thesis tradition — *Keerin was Arceus's first companion, Cormor pact-bonded with Keerin, the Celestica preserved that tradition.* **Canonical PLA's Celestica Arceus-worship is, in this project's cosmology, the surviving fragment of the original cosmic-partnership tradition.**

### Missingno → Phancero `[LOCKED v0.9.4 — one of the project's deepest fan-canon connections]`

**Modern Pokemon canon's most famous glitch is, in this project's cosmology, Phancero's first material incursion.**

**Per Section 2 — Cormorian founding myth:** Phancero slipped a fragment of itself into the world off the coast of Cinnabar Island, originally as "a static, barely corporeal lump of energy." This entity is what canonical Pokemon conspiracy theorists call **Missingno** — the famous glitch phenomenon of the original Red/Blue/Yellow games.

**Why this connection works:**

- Missingno's canonical "glitchy" nature mirrors Phancero's cosmic-shadow identity (glitchy, incorporeal, anti-creation)
- Missingno's canonical "appearance off Cinnabar Island" via the Old Man tutorial-trick mirrors Phancero's first incursion off Cinnabar Island
- Missingno's canonical lack-of-identity in lore (no name, no clear type, no recognized form) mirrors Phancero's *suppressed-name* status — the canonical world *knows* the entity exists but does not have language to name it
- Modern Pokemon canon's discomfort with Missingno (it cannot be properly displayed in modern games; it remains a curiosity-not-canonical-entity) mirrors the *active suppression* of Phancero's name in early Kanto history

**Players who notice this connection will be delighted.** Players who don't still get a complete story. **It is one of the project's most layered fan-canon connections.**

### The Four Lost Birds — Phancero in Early Kanto Pantheon `[LOCKED v0.9.4 — refined]`

In Kanto's earliest historical era, humans worshipped **four** legendary birds: Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, and **Phancero**. **Phancero is known in Kanto's history** as the fourth ancient worshipped bird — but his *name and identity* were suppressed and erased from Kanto's historical record following the events of Cormor + Keerin's pact.

**The framing is precise:**

- *Modern Kanto knows there was a fourth bird worshipped in antiquity* — historical scholars and ancient-religion researchers can find references to a "fourth bird" in old documents
- *Modern Kanto does not know the bird's name* (Phancero) — the suppression of the name is part of Phancero's lasting influence
- *Modern Kanto does not know what happened to the fourth bird* — only that it was once worshipped and is no longer
- *The suppression is institutional* — possibly by early Kanto religious authorities, possibly by an Arceus-aligned tradition, possibly self-imposed by the fading nomadic-tribe carriers who feared the name itself

**This is significant worldbuilding nuance.** Phancero's fourth-bird status is *historical fact* preserved as a hollow shape — an absence in the canonical pantheon that scholars can detect (*"there was a fourth bird, but we don't know its name"*) without recovering the details. **The suppression *itself* is part of Phancero's lasting influence on the world** — even after the erasing, the entity continued to *shape* the world by being unspeakable.

**Implications:**
- Canonical Kanto's Articuno/Zapdos/Moltres trio is the *post-suppression* version of an originally-four-bird pantheon
- Ancient Kanto religious texts likely contain *gaps* where Phancero's references were systematically erased
- Modern Kanto religious traditions may have *fossil-references* to the fourth bird without conscious awareness of what was lost
- The project's Book of the Moon — when read by engaged players — restores the *name* and *identity* of the lost bird, returning what canonical Kanto's institutional suppression took

### Madame Roma / Roma Langerin → all of House Langerin `[LOCKED v0.9.4]`

**Madame Roma is the progenitor of House Langerin** — the founding figure of the entire Cormorian noble house, the source of all the Langerin family's distinctive powers.

**Per Section 7 — Madame Roma entry:**
- Original miko who bargained with both Giratina and Marshadow in ancient times
- Cormor's instrumental co-architect of the pact-era (forged the four objects with him through miko-consecration)
- First person Cormor brought into the fledgling empire as "royal bloodline" with the first Arceus + Keerin doubly-blessed surname
- Founder of House Langerin via her coupling with Lethys (Section 7 — Hermit's Roma-Lethys romance subsection)

**Implications for modern Pokemon canon's House Langerin lineage:**
- Every Langerin descendant — including Kimaris in the present-day story — inherits powers Roma's bargains established
- Marshadow generational ace traces to Roma's original Marshadow bargain
- Mirroh Necropolis Distortion gate guardianship traces to Roma's original Giratina bargain
- After Cormoria's eventual collapse, the Langerin bloodline likely fragments and disperses
- `[OPEN]` Whether any modern Pokemon canon characters descend from House Langerin (likely no direct canonical connection, but possible inspirations exist)

**The hidden tragedy:**

The modern Langerin family does not know that Madame Roma is their progenitor. **Kimaris bonds with his Marshadow without recognizing that the soothsayer who occasionally visits the royal court is his ancestor.** This is the cleanest tragic-irony in the project — *Roma watches her bloodline continue without recognition; the bloodline continues without recognizing her*.

### Mt. Silver → Future-Red Cross-Canon Encounter `[LOCKED v0.9.4]`

**The optional post-Champion Keerin sidequest transports the player to Mt. Silver in Kanto to face a multiverse-displaced future version of canonical Red** (Section 7 — Future-Red entry; Section 9 — Keerin entry).

**Cross-canon elements:**

- **Mt. Silver itself** — the canonical Gold/Silver/Crystal/HG/SS location at the top of Kanto where the strongest trainers test themselves. The Ruination map is visually identical to the canonical version.
- **Future-Red** — an older young-adult version of canonical Red, vastly more powerful than his canonical Gold/Silver appearance, **covered in shadow** suggesting otherworldly corruption or temporal displacement. *Theoretically the strongest version of the character across the Pokemon multiverse.*
- **The "..." dialogue** — Future-Red maintains canonical Red's iconic silence on first encounter, breaking it only after defeat
- **The team of six broken legendaries** — Mewtwo (canonical Red signature), Urshifu Rapid Strike (Galar), Yveltal (Kalos, the Keerin-counter), Mega Rayquaza (Hoenn, ultimate Mega), Eternatus (Galar, galactic-scale threat), Miraidon (Future Paradox from Paldea)

**Why this is one of the project's deepest cross-canon engagements:**

- **It uses canonical Pokemon's most iconic ultimate-trainer-test elements** (Mt. Silver + Red) in a way that respects the canonical material while adding genuinely new content (older corrupted Red with multiverse-team)
- **It establishes Future-Red's existence as a multiverse canon-element** — opening cosmological design space for future projects (canonical or fan) to explore similar concepts
- **It honors the canonical Red character at his highest possible power level** — *the* strongest possible iteration
- **It produces one of the most memorable single sidequests in Pokemon ROM hack history** — players who complete it will remember the moment they faced corrupted future-Red

**The temporal displacement mechanism:**

Per Section 9 — Dreamstone (polarity + time-displacement framework): Dreamstones can be used to open paths through time. Keerin's pact-power transports the player across temporal-cosmological space via this mechanism. The Mt. Silver encounter happens in the *future* relative to Cormoria's present-day timeline (Mt. Silver as a canonical location exists ~2000 years after Cormoria).

**The cross-canon framing:**

> "You must overcome the strongest Trainer of the future in order to have a future of your own." — Keerin to the player, pre-battle

This explicitly invokes the temporal-cosmological gap as a *test*. The player must overcome the strongest expression of canonical Pokemon's future to *earn* their place in cosmological partnership. **Defeating future-Red is the highest mechanical achievement in the project, and it explicitly anchors that achievement to canonical Pokemon's most iconic ultimate-trainer-test.**

- ~~**Player-driven design over mainline canonicity**~~ — **LOCKED in v0.9.8 as a project-level principle**: When user-specified Pokémon kits, abilities, custom moves, or evolution mechanics diverge from mainline canon, the project implements the user's design. Empire-era Cormoria has its own breeding programs and training traditions that diverge from modern-canon Pokémon traits. The auditor's role is to flag *engine concerns*, not *canonicity concerns*. See Section 11 — Principle: Player-Driven Design Over Mainline Canonicity.
- ~~**Motifs are tools, not templates**~~ — **LOCKED in v0.9.8 as a meta-principle**: Project-level design patterns (two-ace structures, Pokémon-Pokémon overworld relationships, generational defensive aces, bloodline-to-modern-canon descents, etc.) are applied where they best serve the character or story. They are not requirements that must apply to every major character. Examples: Kimaris has only Crowley (no second ace); Goma has only Smolder (Mega Houndoom is a combat asset not a bonded ace); Baradus has inverted two-ace (Shardik public + Guzzlord private, no inter-Pokemon relationship). See Section 11 — Principle: Motifs Are Tools, Not Templates.

Narrative structure (what happens at each Trial, in what order) remains locked; only *where* is open. See Section 11 — Principle: Deferred Locations Until Map-Design Session.

Let us meet again."), G4 (same scene as G3 ending — departure line), and G5 (Sandaconda + Scrafty + Turtonator + Dracovish + Shelgon, before Trial 6, with Umbra present; initiates the Hermit-revelation scene). The player observes Glaive's growth in real time via what he brings to each fight — show-don't-tell at its purest. See Section 7 — Glaive arc (restructured v0.9.8).
- ~~**Glaive failure of Garchomp quest as desert-sojourn premise**~~ — **LOCKED in v0.9.8**: Glaive enters the desert between G2 and G3 *pursuing* the legendary Garchomp; he *fails* to acquire it. The failure (combined with the sandstorm rescue by the Hermit and the partnership-training he receives) is what humbles him into the calmer, partnership-coded trainer the player meets at G3. **He returns with Sandaconda (the dragon he met) instead of Garchomp (the legendary he chased).** The Sandaconda's presence at G3 is the player-observable diagnosis of what the desert taught him.

- ~~**Starter Stage-2 → Stage-3 evolution mechanism**~~ — **LOCKED in v0.9.8**: The starter evolves to its Stage-3 600 BST form **via the Blue Moon Hermit's partnership-readiness ritual**, not via a level-up gate. The ritual triggers the dream-Boran trauma fight; victory in the fight triggers the Hermit teaching the signature gating move (Mountain Gale / Blood Moon / Gigaton Hammer); the starter then evolves *at whatever level it is currently at*. **Ritual-gated, not level-gated.** Loss does not punitively gate progression; the player retries until victorious. This is the project's tightest mechanical-narrative weld — the combat victory IS the psychological renunciation IS the evolution unlock. See Section 11 — Mechanical-Narrative Welds principle; Section 6 — starter evolution mechanics; Section 14 — Trial 6 chapter onset.

The phrase resonates forward to Mt. Ceram (Act III) and the Hall of Fame moment. *Show-don't-tell:* Glaive thinks it's babbling; the player sees Umbra's and Osrid's faces register recognition. The mechanic IS the narrative. Paradigmatic example: the Trial 6 chapter onset Hermit ritual + dream-Boran fight + starter Stage-3 evolution — three layers welded into a single event. Other examples: Crabominable adoption mechanic, Sable Shiny Charm sidequest, Z-Bracelet acquisition at Trial 5, Trial 4 doubles-only format. See Section 11 — Principle: Mechanical-Narrative Welds.

Pyrokinesis has diminished across most modern branches; succession follows strict pyrokinetic-strength rules; Reid and Sable are the only living modern Ashlands with active powers. Phlegein's 4th move is **Scorching Sands** (Ground-type special, 30% burn) — closes the Heatran kit's coverage gaps and pairs with Earth Eater (Ground-immune ace with Ground-coverage offense = asymmetric defense).

Ceram raid scene**~~ — **LOCKED in v0.9.8 (narrative; engineering OPEN)**: Player witnesses Reid burn Beads cultists alive to save his sisters, arriving moments too late for conventional Pokemon-battle resolution to prevent it. **The first moment in the game where the partnership thesis fails in real time** — not because it's wrong, but because real violence sometimes outruns it. Flagged as Show-Don't-Tell directness exception (Section 11). Quiet aftermath (Reid does not celebrate, says little). One of the very few on-screen instances of a sympathetic main character killing humans directly — tonal-threshold scene. See Section 14 engineering task #74.

#### v0.9.8 explicit retcon — Glaive-Hermit sandstorm rescue timing

This is the project's first explicitly-documented retcon of a prior version's lock, recorded here so future bible readers and future sessions see the correction in the closure log rather than discover it through file-diff archaeology.

- ~~**Glaive-Hermit sandstorm rescue timing**~~ — **RETCONNED v0.9.7-or-earlier → v0.9.8**: The v0.9.4 framing placed the Hermit-Glaive sandstorm rescue and partnership-training in Glaive's *pre-game wandering years* during Osrid's overseas service. **v0.9.8 corrects this to an on-screen event during the early game** — Glaive's desert sojourn between fights G2 and G3 (during his failed pursuit of the legendary Garchomp). The rescue is *contemporary*, not historical; Glaive's recounting at the Trial 6 chapter onset (Section 14 — Trial 6 chapter G5 scene) is therefore a *recent transformation* he is describing, not a buried memory.
  - **What changes:** the *timing* of the Hermit-Glaive event. Glaive starts the game as a *fledgling* Dragon Master (Bagon + Turtonator only), not a previously-Hermit-trained one. His full team is built up *across the on-screen five-Glaive-fight ladder*, fight by fight. Sandaconda specifically is acquired during the desert sojourn between G2 and G3, alongside the Hermit rescue and the Bagon→Shelgon evolution. **The player observes Glaive's growth in real time**, rather than being told about pre-game development.
  - **What survives unchanged (structural significance preserved):**
    - The Hermit gave Glaive partnership-training that enabled Bagon→Shelgon
    - The Hermit recognized Glaive's psychic-empathic gift before Cadmus Umbra did
    - Cormoria's dragon-tradition is, at its root, downstream of the Hermit's teaching
    - The cross-canon Lance/Blackthorn City descent through Glaive's Dragon's Den order is unchanged
    - The Hermit's broader role as the project's master partnership-teacher is unchanged
    - The Trial 6 chapter onset G5 scene (Glaive recounting the Hermit story to Umbra and the player, leading to the Hermit-quest unlock) is unchanged in *structure* — only the *register* of Glaive's recounting changes from "buried-history" to "recent-transformation."
  - **Files updated in v0.9.8 to enact the retcon:** `bible/07_characters_viziers.md` (Glaive arc fully restructured), `bible/11_characters_legendary.md` (Hermit Function-2 entry rewritten), `bible/15_design_principles.md` (Glaive's-overworld-interactions reference corrected), `bible/17_open_questions.md` (v0.9.4 RESOLVED entry annotated + this explicit retcon entry added). See git history for the consistency-repair commit.
  - **Why the retcon:** the on-screen real-time framing aligns better with the project's *show-don't-tell* writing principle (Section 11 — Principle: Show, Don't Tell, locked v0.9.8). The player observes Glaive's transformation through *what he brings to combat across five fights* rather than being told about it via exposition. This is one of the clearest applications of the show-don't-tell principle in the project's character architecture.

## 14. Production Discipline

Story design and engineering proceed in parallel from v0.5 onward. The validation phase is complete (a prior Claude session verified the pipeline through real feature work). Every design decision continues to be one we can actually build.

### Pipeline status as of v0.9.3

**v0.9.3 is the post-Champion Ancient Cormoria side quests detail-lock patch** — touching Sections 6, 7, 13, 14. Key v0.9.3 additions:

- **Baxcaliburite quest ("The Origins of Cormoria's Dragons") fully specified** — Glaive accompanies the player; cave with ice puzzle; both the Baxcaliburite and Salamencite are discovered; **2v2 double battle Mega Baxcalibur + Mega Salamence vs. Roaring Moon + Walking Wake at level 120** (above-cap). Functions as the pre-cursor to the Sword Cult HQ raid + 7v9 final battle.
- **Ancient Peat Block quest ("The Shadow Self") fully specified** — the Blue Moon Hermit accompanies the player; ancient fog-shrouded Cormorian swamp setting (not a cave); **6v6 mirror match against the player's own shadow-self** with an identical-team opponent. Tests pure execution and outplaying.
- **Divine Cuirass quest ("The Sleeping Terror") fully specified** — *solo quest*; multi-floor puzzle temple where Koraidon sleeps; Hoopa Unbound guardian; **5-stage continuous gauntlet** (Blacephalon → Galarian Moltres → Iron Moth → Hoopa Unbound → Koraidon, all at level 100). Toughest combat encounter in the project outside the 7v9 final battle.
- **Glaive's Mega Salamence acquisition** locked as a byproduct of the Frigibax-picker's Baxcaliburite quest. Glaive faces Roaring Moon — the *Past Paradox version of his own Salamence*.
- **The Blue Moon Hermit** locked as a recurring named character — Trial 6 Master Tutor (teaches Blood Moon Ground for Bloodmoon Ursaluna evolution) + post-Champion Ancient Peat Block quest companion. *One character, two appearances*; consolidates a previously-open NPC identity.
- **Comparison table of the three side quests** locked across all distinguishing axes (setting, companion, combat structure, opponent count, emotional register, test of player skill, reward).
- **Above-cap encounter precedent established** — Roaring Moon and Walking Wake at level 120 are the first formally-locked above-cap encounters in the project; sets the design pattern for exceptional set-piece combat.

**v0.9.2 (preceding)** locked the Blue Moon Teddiursa line identity, the trio's offensive/defensive trinity, Frigibax/Tinkatink/Teddiursa ability suites, Blood Moon (Ground) custom move modification, Lunacy custom ability, Ancient Peat Block consumable, and the two-mechanic separation (Trial 6 Master Tutor evolution gates vs. post-Champion Ancient Cormoria side quests).

**v0.9.1 (preceding)** locked the Nobility Concordance senate structure, Leyline Resonance phenomenon, Cult Cosmological Framework (three conditions + Arceus-avoidance + Dreamstone-fragment failure), Domdaniel (House Moray's generational ace), Brie Moray full entry, Silas's Domdaniel-rejection wound, Nemo's secret-savior recharacterization, Baradus's three-fears framework, Goma's envy framing, Sylphon & Stone full status + Silph Co / Devon Corp descendants, Marshadow's Necropolis-Assault late-game deployment, and the Cormoria-as-mother-region note.

**v0.9 (preceding) was the Rhydia culmination patch** locking the original-purpose Rhydia character work and substantial worldbuilding (Cormor Dream-Eater origin, Justice's Iron Valiant truth, Generational Aces tier-system, Cormorian institutions).

**v0.8.2 (preceding)** locked the Hall of Fame unmasking sequence, the renunciation-not-amnesia epilogue framing, House Alban as Osrid's overseas cover identity, and the "Nomad" cultural designation.

**v0.8.1 (preceding)** locked the military rank hierarchy, surname-as-sacrament rule, House Surge, Manus Surge as 3rd Trial Baron, the ~50% Rhydia-learns-the-truth beat, and the Boran-Surge-to-Lt-Surge bloodline.

**v0.8 (preceding) was the largest single bible expansion** — Templar Arceus order, Tavern Pokemon Centers, Braviary travel, full Silas/Pierra/Baradus rewrites, Trial Barons Kimaris/Reid/Nemo, Sable Ashland, Mt. Ceram → Ancient Cormoria → Koraidon beat, the 7v9 final battle, Crabominable adoption, Ravage move, Mega Evolution policy, the Aerodactylite singular relic, and Cross-fandom References.

**Architecture note `[OPEN]`:** The bible is now approaching 2000 lines as a single document. At ~2500 lines this likely becomes unwieldy. We may need to split into multiple documents in a future revision:
- **World Bible** (Sections 1-4, 9, 11-12) — setting, institutions, mechanics, design principles, canon connections
- **Story Bible** (Sections 5-8, 10, 13) — characters, cults, story spine, open questions

### Process discipline (carried forward from v0.4 + handoff doc + Frigibax work)

The handoff doc consolidates patterns we should follow. Highest-priority disciplines:

- **Read before editing.** `grep -rn <identifier>` first. The same data often lives in multiple files (enum + initializer + JSON); editing one without the others creates silent bugs.
- **Verify constants exist** before referencing them. This fork has custom items, abilities, and species. Never assume vanilla pokeemerald constants exist.
- **For sprite/palette work:** analyze the sprite's actual per-index pixel mapping (front and back separately if they differ) before designing a palette. Don't apply the same auto-recolor to both battle and overworld palettes — they have different index meanings. Preview visually before committing.
- **Pre-quantize palette colors to multiples of 8** for GBA-safe rendering. This ensures the preview matches the in-game result exactly.
- **Delete compiled `.gbapal` / `.4bpp` / `.lz` binaries** when changing their source `.pal` / `.png`. Stale binaries can confuse incremental builds. Issue clear "delete these files" instructions alongside any patch that changes source palette/sprite files.
- **Edit BOTH `.pory` and `.inc`** for map scripts. GenSpark's build may or may not regenerate `.inc` from `.pory`; editing both is cheap insurance.
- **For player-facing questions** (catchable? reachable map? NPC exists?), authority order is: user's experience → DM Dex spreadsheet → handoff doc → source tree → engine docs → canon.
- **When questions can be answered by running a command in the repo, run the command** rather than asking the user.
- **For sprite recolor work, always render preview PNGs and get user sign-off before producing a patch.** Iteration in design space is faster than iteration in compile space.

49. **Engine type-effectiveness override — Behemoth Blade (Fairy override)** — `[SMALL — engine code]`
    - Behemoth Blade is implemented as Dragon-type, 120 BP, physical, 10 PP, learned at Lv 77 by Baxcalibur.
    - The engineering need: damage calculator hook so that against a **Fairy-type** target, the move resolves as super-effective (2×) regardless of the calculated Dragon-vs-Fairy 0× immunity that would otherwise apply.
    - Pattern: parallel to the existing **Freeze-Dry** override (Ice-type move with super-effective override vs. Water).
    - Implementation location: `src/battle_util.c` damage-modifier path; gate via a new `MOVE_EFFECT_*` flag on the move data entry.
    - Localization: move-description text should note the special-effectiveness behavior.
    - Estimated scope: ~30 lines across 2–3 files.

50. **Engine type-effectiveness override — Behemoth Bash (Steel override)** — `[SMALL — engine code]`
    - Behemoth Bash is implemented as Normal-type physical, 100 BP, 95% acc, 10 PP, learned at Lv 30 by Tinkatuff (carried to Tinkaton).
    - The engineering need: damage calculator hook so that against a **Steel-type** target, the move resolves as super-effective (2×) regardless of its Normal-type resolution (including post-Pixilate Fairy resolution).
    - This task supersedes the "New MOVE_EFFECT flag for Steel-effectiveness override" bullet inside task #36 above — that bullet described the same hook; this entry tracks it as standalone post-landing.
    - Pattern: parallel to Freeze-Dry.

    - Estimated scope: ~30 lines across 2–3 files.

    - **Common scripting template.** A single reusable `.pory` macro/script template that takes per-character parameters (trainer overworld object ID, ace species, ace overworld object ID, dialogue text array, emoticon type) and produces the standard 3-beat interaction: emoticon-over-trainer-head → dialogue line(s) → ace cry → optional emoticon-over-ace-head. Reuse across all 23 characters' interactions.
    - **Proximity-trigger system.** Player walks within N tiles of trainer+ace pair → interaction fires. Should be configurable per-instance: some interactions are proximity-triggered (background flavor), others are scripted-scene-triggered (cutscene moments). Both modes should use the same underlying template.
    - **Non-blocking-cutscene design.** The interaction should *not* freeze the player's movement; the player should be able to walk past the interaction as it plays out. Avoids the "every NPC stops you with a story" anti-pattern of older Pokémon games.
    - **Per-interaction cooldown.** Prevent the same interaction from re-firing every time the player passes by. Recommended: 1-time-per-area-load, or once-per-day-cycle, configurable per instance.

    **Estimated scope:** ~20-40 hours one-time engine work (~10-15 hours if pokeemerald-expansion already has most of the primitives in place; ~30-40 hours if multiple primitives need to be built from scratch).

The event is **required main-story progression** (not a side quest); the player cannot face Trial 6 without completing it (loss does not gate progression in the conventional way — the player can retry until they win, but the starter cannot evolve and Trial 6 cannot be faced until they do).

    **Components:**
    - **Placement:** Trial 6 chapter, between the G5 Glaive-Umbra-Osrid scene (task #64) and the Trial 6 Baron fight. **Trigger:** the player reaches the Blue Moon Hermit's location and accepts the partnership-readiness ritual.
    - **Custom sprite for Boran:** overworld NPC sprite + trainer-battle sprite (Windshear-rank ceremonial mask iconography per Section 7 — Cormorian military rank hierarchy); stylized to read as *dream-sequence-aesthetic* (washed colors, soft edges, surreal framing).
    - **Custom dream-sequence visual treatment:** battle background and transition effects styled to signal *this is not the present, this is Osrid's interior*. Sepia/desaturated palette, fog effects, no normal Cormoria geography in the background.
    - **Boran's team:** `[OPEN]` (intentionally *unremarkable, military-effective, without bond-shaped optimization* — what hyper-competent training looks like *without* partnership). Difficulty calibrated to Trial 6 cap (45) at peer-level.
    - **Osrid's team in the dream:** the player's *current* team — preserves agency, makes the dream feel *now* rather than *then*.
    - **Pre-/post-battle dialogue:** Boran addresses his student (using "Nomad"); references the starter-specific signature move being unlocked (Mountain Gale / Blood Moon / Gigaton Hammer); dialog resonates with Osrid's internal arc.
    - **Win-condition consequence:** beating dream-Boran *unlocks the starter Stage-2 → Stage-3 evolution* (the Hermit teaches the signature move, the starter evolves to its 600 BST form at current level). This is the project's tightest mechanical-narrative weld — the combat victory IS the psychological renunciation (Section 11 — Principle: Mechanical-Narrative Welds, locked v0.9.8).
    - **Loss-condition behavior:** ritual ends without evolution; brief Boran-worldview-reinforced dialog ("You are not ready"); player can retry. Repeated losses are not punished — they simply mean *continued effort to overcome the trauma*.
    - **Boran is NOT in the ace-bonding pattern** — see Section 7 / Section 11 anti-pattern characterization.
    - **Estimated scope:** ~12-18 hours (custom sprite + dream-sequence visual effects + Boran team data + scripted event + dialog authoring with starter-branching + Hermit-ritual scene scripting + Stage-3 evolution scripted event).
    - **Cross-references:** Section 7 — Boran Surge, Section 7 — Blue Moon Hermit, Section 11 — Mechanical-Narrative Welds principle, Section 11 — Ace-Bonding anti-pattern, Section 14 — Trial 6 chapter onset sequence, Section 5 — Osrid's psychological arc, Section 6 — starter Stage-3 evolution mechanics.

    - **Set accuracy to 80** (canonical Population Bomb is 90)
    - **Set PP to 2** (canonical Population Bomb is 10) — balancing constraint; Falco can use Bombard at most twice per Trial 5 fight

    - **Engine considerations:** with Skill Link (Drang's ability), Bombard attempts all 10 hits; on a hit-confirm roll the move lands; on a miss the entire move misses. **Lock-On set on Drang the prior turn raises Bombard's effective accuracy to 100%** — this is the design's central tactical pressure.
    - **Estimated scope:** ~10-15 lines move-data entry + animation table update + testing

74. **Reid Ashland Mt. Ceram raid pyrokinesis scene — implementation** — `[MEDIUM-LARGE — custom assets + scripting + dialog]`

    Per Section 7 — Reid Ashland (v0.9.8 lock) and Section 14 — Mt. Ceram raid Act III. One of the project's most morally weighty scenes and a tonal-threshold beat (first on-screen instance of a sympathetic main character killing humans directly).

    **Components:**
    - **Trigger:** during the Mt. Ceram raid Act III sequence, after the player has fought through some early Beads cultist encounters with Reid (the "minutes that mattered" delay)
    - **Custom sprites for Rain, Brook, and River Ashland:** the three sisters need overworld sprites for this scene (their first on-screen appearance — `[OPEN]` whether they appear in earlier Ashland Labyrinth scenes for sister familiarity before the danger lands; recommended yes, brief earlier scene)
    - **Custom pyrokinesis visual effect:** Reid materializing/directing fire. **NOT a Pokemon move animation** — this is a *human-side* supernatural-power effect, visually distinct from Pokemon-based fire moves. Design language: more *embodied* and *intimate* than a Pokemon flamethrower (Reid's hands or stance generating the fire directly).
    - **Cultist-burned visual treatment:** the on-screen aftermath of the burn. **Restraint matters here** — the project crosses a tonal threshold but should not become gratuitous. Recommendation: brief, decisive, the cultists are *gone* without dwelling on graphic gore. The horror is in the act and the aftermath, not the spectacle.
    - **The "moments-too-late" pacing:** the scene's emotional center depends on the player feeling that they arrived *just too late*. Pacing of the immediately-preceding cultist encounters must reinforce this — *the player should feel the time running out*.
    - **Aftermath dialog and silence:** Reid does not celebrate, does not speak much. Brief dialog (recommend minimal — *"I had hoped never to use this power that way"* or similar). Sister reactions (relief, fear, gratitude in different mixtures). Player has dialog options or quiet observation `[OPEN]`.
    - **Engine considerations:** scripted cutscene with custom visual effects; no recurring engine modification needed beyond the visual-effect asset. Tone-and-pacing is the design challenge, not the engine.
    - **Estimated scope:** ~15-25 hours (custom sister sprites + custom pyrokinesis visual effect + scripted scene + dialog + scene pacing tuning; tone restraint is the key constraint)
    - **Cross-references:** Section 7 — Reid Ashland, Section 12 — House Ashland Naljo lore (the family's foundational moral identity that this scene resonates with), Section 11 — Show-Don't-Tell directness exceptions (v0.9.8 lock), Section 14 — Mt. Ceram raid Act III, Section 8 — Beads Cult Mt. Ceram raid

### v0.9.10 new engineering tasks (Ambrosia quest + stat-rivals reward)

- **Six Ambrosia Drop items (color-keyed, cap-bypassing EV-max)** `[LOCKED v0.9.10]` — Add six consumable items: Green (HP), Red (Attack), Yellow (Defense), Purple (Sp.Atk), Blue (Sp.Def), Pink (Speed). Art is one base "Ambrosia Drop" icon + six palette swaps (color is the only differentiator). One shared out-of-battle item routine keyed to stat that **sets** the target stat's EVs to `MAX_PER_STAT_EVS` (252) in a single use.
  - **Cap-bypass scope (verified):** `B_EV_ITEMS_CAP == FALSE` (`codebase/include/config/caps.h:31`), so the EV-item path caps at `MAX_TOTAL_EVS` (510), *not* the badge-scaled `GetCurrentEVCap()`. The Drop therefore only needs to skip the 510 total check at `src/pokemon.c:3912`; `GetCurrentEVCap()` never touches the item path unless `B_EV_ITEMS_CAP` is later flipped to TRUE (then the bypass must also skip it). Keep the 252 per-stat clamp at `src/pokemon.c:5472` intact — no stat exceeds 252, but the six-stat total may reach 1512.
  - **Waste guard:** the Drops are finite (six in the whole game), so the item must refuse or warn when the target stat is already at 252 — a player must never silently burn one for zero gain.
  - **Awarding:** 1:1 from the six stat-rivals on defeat during the Ambrosia quest. Design/lore spec lives in Section 15 (*The Ambrosia Quest — Structure & Reward*); this entry is the implementation task.

### Evernahn tileset conversion (Pelluca prerequisite) `[build task]`

The Pelluca Valley map (§16.3) is painted from the **Evernahn** tileset, which currently exists only as **RMXP-format source**, now committed at `assets/pelluca_tileset_source/` (`Evernahn.png` + grass/water autotiles, `Calvera_Water*.png`, and the RMXP `Map005/Map588/Tilesets.rxdata`). It must be converted to pokeemerald format before any Pelluca tiles can be placed — the **hard prerequisite** for the whole map build.

**The core constraint:** the RMXP set is ~1544 tiles at **32×32px**, but pokeemerald uses **16×16px metatiles** with a hard budget (~512 primary + ~512 secondary metatiles per map, 16-color sub-palettes, max 2 tilesets per map). So it is not a straight import; it needs:
1. **Downscale** 32px → 16px per tile (a mode/nearest downscale keeps flatter blocks than smoothing — same lesson as the sprite work).
2. **Palette fit** — quantize each tileset to the 16-color sub-palette budget.
3. **Primary/secondary split** — partition into a shared **primary** tileset (ground/common) + a Pelluca-specific **secondary** tileset, cutting/merging redundant tiles to stay under the metatile budget.
4. **Import via Porymap** — build metatile definitions + attributes; the map then paints from them.

The `.rxdata` files are RMXP source (not directly usable in pokeemerald) — they hold the original Evernahn maps/tileset definitions and are kept as the conversion reference.

## 15. Cormoria Location Atlas `[v0.9.10]`

### 15.1 Purpose and the DM relationship

This section is the canonical geographic reference for empire-era Cormoria — the region layout, every major location, its story/trial role, its connections, and its **DM-fate** (what it becomes in Dreamstone Mysteries). It was established from the illustrated empire-era region map developed with the design partner, cross-referenced against DM's actual codebase map (`region_map_sections.json` + the outdoor connection graph) and against the rest of this bible.

**The core relationship (locked — Sections 1, 12):** Dreamstone Ruination is the *prequel* — empire-era Cormoria, ~2,000–3,000 years before DM. **DM's Cormoria is the same land, aged and fallen.** An end-game region-wide tectonic **calamity** (15.3) reshapes the continent into DM's diminished modern layout. Consequences:
- **Empires fall.** An imperial city in our era may be a base camp, ruin, graveyard, or wilderness in DM (rarely the reverse).
- **Base camps ← cities.** DM's Ceram/Mirroh Base Camps and Rivetshore are the remnants of larger empire settlements.
- **DM's "Ancient" maps are windows into our era** — Ancient Ceram/Mirroh (and an Ancient Cormoria finale), reached via dreamstone time-travel.
- **The empire is larger** — we add locations DM doesn't have.

**Status conventions used below:**
- `[LOCKED]` — venue/fact already fixed elsewhere in the bible.
- `[LOCKED v0.9.10]` — placement decided in the region-map design session.
- `[PROPOSED]` — assistant proposal, not yet confirmed by the design partner.
- `[OPEN]` — undecided.

### 15.2 Region overview

Empire-era Cormoria is a single large landmass with an island-studded southern coast (compass N up). The player's journey begins at the **Pelluca Valley** nexus in the south-center and radiates along four arms:
- **North** — up the **Ivy River** into the marshlands.
- **West** — around to the haunted **Mirroh** massif and the **Necropolis** (Trial 1).
- **East** — along the **Hoya River Delta**, through the **Shadowmarshes**, to the eastern frontier.
- **South** — through wetlands to **Rivetshore** and (via the Riptide Bridge) **Windrunner Island**.

Biome gradient: a wet green heartland (Ivy marshlands, Hoya delta, Shadowmarshes, southern wetlands) drying eastward into the arid **Seregmorn Desert** and the cracked volcanic **Ashlands** around **Mt. Ceram**. Snow caps the **Mirroh** massif in the northwest. The capital, **Silversun**, sits elevated in the north.

### 15.3 The calamity (end-game tectonic event) `[LOCKED v0.9.10 — framing]`

At the climax, a region-wide **tectonic cataclysm** (the "sealing cataclysm," Section 10) shatters and reshapes the continent; almost everything is rebuilt over the following centuries into DM's smaller, diminished Cormoria. Design links:
- **Ting-Lu connection.** The quake reads naturally as tied to **Ting-Lu** (the Ground/Dark Treasure of Ruin), which is physically present in the Trial 9 fight (Nemo Korolev). `[OPEN — is the calamity Ting-Lu-caused/epicentered, and is Mt. Mirroh Peak (T9) the epicenter?]`
- **DM-fate.** Each location below carries its post-calamity DM outcome where known (15.7).

### 15.4 Locations by region

#### The Central Nexus
- **Pelluca Valley** `[LOCKED v0.9.10]` — *(central; the START)* — empire-era city / large rural seaside fishing settlement. The **Umbra family domain**: Cadmus Umbra's estate, his **laboratories**, and his **Academy** (where he is resident headmaster; the six stat-rivals' alma mater — distinct from Northpoint). Also hosts the **deep-cavern** sidequest (third Jousteel egg; Umbra-sealed water/ice descent; taken by the Crawdaunt-clan water cult) — likely an indoor map off the valley. Four-way nexus (N Ivy River, W Mirroh, E Hoya Delta, S Rivetshore). **The player (Osrid, "Nomad") begins here.** DM-fate: **Pelluca City**.

#### The West — the cosmological corner
Ground zero of the mythology: it *begins* (Hollow Hill), *threatens to re-erupt* (Necropolis Distortion gate), and *climaxes* (Mt. Mirroh Peak / Ting-Lu). Wants a consistent haunted/spectral aesthetic across the cluster.
- **Mirroh** `[LOCKED v0.9.10]` — *(west)* — the haunted city on the Mirroh massif; House Langerin's seat-adjacent settlement. DM-fate: aged into the **Mirroh Base Camp** area.
- **Mirroh Necropolis** `[LOCKED]` — *(west, on the massif)* — **Trial 1 venue** (Kimaris Langerin, Ghost, Wraith, cap 18); Langerin-family keepers. Adjacent **Necropolis Distortion gate** — canon's likeliest Phancero *re-entry* point, near Chien-Pao's incarnation site. The Act VI Necropolis Assault + sealing cataclysm centers here. DM-fate: **Mirroh Base Camp Graveyard**.
- **Hollow Hill** `[LOCKED v0.9.10 — placement]` — *(west, SW of Mirroh; connects off the Mirroh cluster)* — a fog-bound, forested, spectral-energy hill that draws Ghost-types. **Forgotten significance:** the site where **Cormor Dream-Eater erased Phancero** and where the four objects were corrupted into the **Treasures of Ruin** by Phancero's residual contamination (Section 1). *Consistency note:* Phancero was **erased, not sealed** — Hollow Hill is the battle/ritual *site*, not a prison; the deep lore is lost in the present, so no one connects the curse to the founding event.
- **Mt. Mirroh** `[LOCKED v0.9.10]` — *(west)* — the snow-capped massif: Templar HQ and the Necropolis on its slopes, the city of Mirroh + Hollow Hill at its base, the Peak above. DM-fate: **Mt. Mirroh**.
